newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-LIONS SPOILT FOR CHOICE, CLAIMS MCGEECHAN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LIONS SPOILT FOR CHOICE, CLAIMS MCGEECHAN.

text.p: Coach Ian McGeechan claimed there were still 30 players in contention for a British Lions test place after Tuesday's 51-22 victory over the Emerging Springboks in Welllington.
The Lions' selectors were to pick their side on Tuesday night for the first test against South Africa in Cape Town on Saturday. It will not be announced publicly until shortly before kick-off.
"We are probably looking at 30 players for a place in the test side," said McGeechan of his 35-player squad.
"We have to sit down and look at what we want to put together for Saturday. I think it will be a long meeting."
The victory was the Lions' seventh in eight tour matches to date -- their only loss coming to Northern Transvaal a week last Saturday.

Full-back Tim Stimpson re-stated his case for the number 15 shirt ahead of Neil Jenkins with a superb kicking display which saw him land nine out of 11 kicks at goal and claim 26 points overall including one of the Lions' six tries.
McGeechan added: "We have a lot of decisions to make simply because everyone has been playing well and we have to be fair to all the players.
"We have some comparisons to make and things to look at. We may deliberate until Saturday," he joked.
In Tuesday's game the Lions saw a 13-0 lead after 11 minutes evaporate as they went to the interval leading by just one point, 16-15.
"As soon as we stopped working in the first half, it looked bloody awful," said McGeechan.
"But I take my hat off to the players and their attitude and the fact that they have total trust in each other which is very important."
Emerging Springbok coach Nick Mallett -- Springbok forwards coach last season -- said: "We were very disorganised in defence at times and the Lions shouldn't take too much heart from that.
"They will come up against a side who are much more organised in that area on Saturday."
